source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: According to the lecture, which part of a plain chat session plays the role of the student's own memory in the 'no pencils or pens' analogy?

options.text: The model's training data, learned once and fixed before the conversation ever starts
options.feedback: Training data is fixed and does not change during a conversation, so it cannot play the role of something that fills up and runs out the way the analogy describes. The analogy is about the conversation itself, not what the model learned beforehand.

options.text: Notes the user happens to keep somewhere outside the chat
options.feedback: The analogy is about what the chat session itself has access to, not what the user personally keeps elsewhere. A chat session cannot read a user's outside notes on its own.

options.text: The current context window, which has to hold everything the conversation needs
options.feedback: Just as the student in the analogy can only hold what fits in memory, a chat session can only work with what fits inside its current context window -- there is no external place for it to set anything aside.

options.text: A separate file the chat automatically saves after every message
options.feedback: A plain chat session does not automatically save separate files; that kind of externalized storage is exactly what an agent adds and a chat session lacks, which is the whole point of the analogy.
